title: Google's Cogentic AI Claims Six New Math Proofs
dek: An AI agent on Gemini 4 wrote every paper, but none is peer reviewed yet.

caption:
An AI just claimed to prove something mathematicians have assumed for decades. 🧮

Google Research posted six new Cogentic math papers to GitHub, all written by an AI agent running on Gemini 4 with no human help beyond the first prompt. The headline claim is a proven L[1/3] bound for integer factoring, closing a gap that has stood since Lenstra and Pomerance's L[1/2] result in 1992. Other papers tackle Nash equilibria, the log-rank conjecture and Harary's edge-reconstruction conjecture.

The catch: none of it is peer reviewed, and the promised Lean 4 proofs aren't public yet. The proven constant of 105 is also far too large to threaten real encryption, so your data is safe.

At AI Parabellum we think verification is the real story here. Will machine-checked proofs back these claims up?
